item.title: Self Care
item.description:
Notes on:

  • Fashion: Developing a personal style, curating a wardrobe, and exploring fashion trends.
  • Grooming: Hair care, skincare, makeup, and personal hygiene routines.
  • Self-presentation: Body language, posture, and non-verbal communication.
  • Personal branding: Creating a consistent and authentic personal brand across online and offline platforms.

Quantified Self

  • Outfits worn per week
  • Items purchased (clothing, accessories, grooming products)
  • Money spent on fashion and grooming
  • Skincare routine consistency (days followed)
  • Haircare products used
  • Gym clothes vs. casual clothes ratio
  • Outfit changes per day
  • Laundry cycles completed
  • Dry cleaning visits
  • Tailoring or alterations done
  • Perfume/cologne bottles owned
  • Shoes owned vs. shoes worn
  • Capsules or coordinated outfits created
  • Seasonal wardrobe updates completed
  • Thrifted or second-hand items purchased
  • Impulse fashion purchases tracked
  • Clothing returns made
  • Donation boxes filled

Fashion

Developing a Personal Style

  • Identifying colour palettes that suit your skin tone
  • Understanding body types and what flatters them
  • Building a capsule wardrobe
  • Mixing high and low street pieces
  • Learning when to follow trends and when to ignore them

Wardrobe Essentials

The Basics

  • Well-fitting white t-shirts
  • Dark denim jeans
  • Black or navy chinos
  • A fitted blazer
  • A quality leather jacket
  • White sneakers
  • Black boots
  • A neutral knit sweater

Seasonal Additions

  • Lightweight coat for spring
  • Waterproof jacket for rain
  • Wool overcoat for winter
  • Linen shirts for summer

Shopping Smart

  • Buying less, buying better
  • Knowing your measurements before shopping online
  • Checking fabric composition (natural fibres tend to last longer)
  • Looking for sales and end-of-season clearances
  • Investing in tailoring — a £20 alteration can transform a £50 garment

Caring for Your Clothes

  • Washing less frequently (jeans, knitwear)
  • Using garment bags for storage
  • Learning basic sewing — button replacement, hemming
  • Proper shoe care (polishing, waterproofing)
  • Rotating shoes to extend their life

Grooming

Skincare

The Basics

  • Cleanser — morning and night
  • Moisturiser — suited to your skin type
  • Sunscreen — every day, even when it’s cloudy
  • Exfoliator — once or twice a week

Going Further

  • Serums (vitamin C, retinol, hyaluronic acid)
  • Eye cream
  • Face mask (clay, hydrating, exfoliating)
  • Lip balm
  • Hand cream

Skin Types and What Works

  • Oily skin: gel-based cleansers, oil-free moisturisers
  • Dry skin: cream cleansers, richer moisturisers, facial oils
  • Combination skin: balancing products, targeted treatment
  • Sensitive skin: fragrance-free, minimal ingredient lists

Haircare

  • Finding a barber or stylist you trust
  • Understanding your hair type (straight, wavy, curly, coily)
  • Washing frequency — most people wash too often
  • Conditioner is not optional
  • Scalp health matters — dry scalp means itchy scalp
  • Trimming regularly even if you’re growing it out
  • Product selection — pomade, clay, cream, sea salt spray

Personal Hygiene

  • Daily shower or bath
  • Deodorant — clinical strength if needed
  • Nail care — trimmed, clean, under control
  • Nose and ear hair trimming
  • Oral hygiene — flossing, tongue scraping, mouthwash
  • Foot care — exfoliation, moisturising, proper socks

Makeup (for Those Who Wear It)

  • Skincare first — makeup sits better on healthy skin
  • Less is more for everyday
  • Setting spray extends wear
  • Removing makeup properly before bed

Self-Presentation

Posture

  • Shoulders back, chin level
  • Standing with weight evenly distributed
  • Sitting without slouching — core engaged
  • The wall test: heels, calves, shoulders, head against a wall

Body Language

  • Eye contact — confident but not staring
  • Open gestures — avoid crossing arms defensively
  • Handshakes — firm, brief, dry
  • Mirroring — subtly matching the other person’s energy
  • Personal space — respecting boundaries

Voice and Speech

  • Speaking clearly and at a moderate pace
  • Avoiding vocal fry and uptalk
  • Pausing instead of filling silence with “um”
  • Matching your tone to the situation

Dressing for the Occasion

  • Knowing the dress code before you arrive
  • When in doubt, slightly overdressed beats underdressed
  • Fit matters more than brand
  • Clean, intact shoes go a long way

Personal Branding

Online Presence

  • LinkedIn — professional, updated, with a proper photo
  • Social media — what would you want a potential employer to find?
  • Consistent name and photo across platforms
  • A personal website or portfolio if relevant

Offline Presence

  • How you introduce yourself
  • Your email signature
  • Business cards (yes, still)
  • Consistency between what you say and how you present yourself

The Throughline

Your personal brand isn’t something you manufacture — it’s the consistent thread between who you are and how you show up. It emerges from repeated actions, not a single curated moment.

item.title: Personal Development
item.description:
This is where I keep notes on the things I’m trying to figure out about myself. Self-awareness, goal-setting, habits that actually stick, the occasional crisis of direction — all of it.

It’s not a particularly polished collection. Some entries are finished thoughts, others are just fragments I’m sitting with. That’s fine by me.

Self-Awareness

Understanding yourself isn’t about grand revelations. It’s usually the small, inconvenient things you notice about yourself when you’re not paying attention — the way you react when someone interrupts you, the tasks you consistently avoid, the people who drain you without you realising it until later.

item.title: Self Promotion at Work
item.description:
I used to think self-promotion meant bragging. Turns out it just means making sure the right people know what you’ve done. There’s a difference, and learning it changed how I move through my career.

The people who get promoted aren’t always the best workers. They’re the ones whose work gets seen. That’s not a conspiracy — it’s just how organisations work. If nobody knows you shipped the thing that saved the quarter, you’re not going to get the promotion.

item.title: Spirituality
item.description:
I’ve been thinking a lot about spirituality lately. Not in the abstract, philosophical sense — more like the practical, daily kind. The kind that shows up when you’re sitting in a room full of people and feel completely alone, or when you’re walking through a forest and suddenly remember to breathe.

This page is where I’m collecting my thoughts on the subject. It covers religion, philosophy, meditation, and everything in between. Some of it is personal, some of it is research, and some of it is just me trying to figure things out as I go.

item.title: Your Playbook for an Amazing Life
item.description:
Chapter 1.0 - What is an Amazing Life?

As we embark on our journey of self-discovery and personal growth, one of the fundamental questions we must confront is: What is an amazing life? This question, simple as it may seem, has profound implications. The answer is not only a reflection of our beliefs, values, and priorities, but it also influences our actions and decisions. It is the lighthouse that guides us when we are lost at sea, the North Star that helps us navigate our way through the complexities of existence.
